title: Appropriations Standoff Threatens a Shutdown
summary: Four appropriations bills are stalled over a spending dispute the leadership says it cannot resolve without you.
briefing_text: Four of the twelve appropriations bills remain unresolved with nineteen days until the continuing resolution lapses. The dispute is narrow in substance and wide in symbolism: roughly nine billion dollars across two accounts that both sides have made a test of the new administration. Leadership in both chambers has signalled privately that a deal exists, and neither is willing to move first. A lapse would furlough non-essential functions and cost the economy more than the contested accounts are worth.

cabinet_assessment.state: A lapse would suspend assessed contributions and delay two treaty ratifications, Mr. President. Our partners read a shutdown as a statement about American reliability, fairly or not.
cabinet_assessment.defense: If the continuing resolution lapses I stop flying hours and steaming days within three weeks, sir. That is the whole of my position and I would rather state it once than repeat it in testimony.
cabinet_assessment.treasury: The scoring will decide the vote count more than the rhetoric will. Give me forty-eight hours with the committee staff and I can make the contested accounts smaller than they look.
cabinet_assessment.nsa: A visibly divided Washington is itself a signal to adversaries. Whatever you choose, choose it with the appearance of command.
cabinet_assessment.chief_of_staff: I have the whip count and it is tighter than the leadership admits, sir. Spending capital here means not spending it in the spring, and you only get one spring.
cabinet_assessment.intelligence: I can brief the intelligence committees in closed session today. A lapse interrupts three collection programmes that are difficult to restart cleanly.

choices.label: Cut a Bipartisan Deal
choices.description: Split the difference on the contested accounts and get the bills to your desk before the deadline.

advisor_positions.treasury: It costs eighteen billion over the profile, Mr. President, and it buys a functioning government. I would take that trade today.
advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: You will be accused of caving by people who cannot count votes. The bills pass, which is the only metric that survives the week.

headline.title: The Deal Everyone Signed and Nobody Will Defend

choices.outcome_text: The bills cleared with four days to spare and eighteen billion more than the White House had requested. Both leaders claimed victory on camera and neither made eye contact.

choices.label: Issue a Veto Threat
choices.description: State publicly that any bill containing the contested provisions will be vetoed.

advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: It works if you are prepared to actually veto, Mr. President. If you are not, do not say it, because they will find out within the week.
advisor_positions.defense: A lapse costs me readiness I cannot buy back in the same fiscal year, sir. I will support the position and I want that consequence on the record.

memory.action: appropriations lapsed after the veto threat

choices.outcome_text: The Statement of Administration Policy went out at four in the afternoon and used the word veto twice. The Speaker's office responded in eleven minutes, and not in kind.

advisor_positions.state: I would keep the foreign consequences of a lapse in the address, sir. It is the argument that travels furthest with people who do not follow appropriations.

advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: Every future negotiation starts from this precedent, sir. They will remember exactly how long it took you to fold.
